transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Emerald CTO), Markus Voss (DevOps), Sara Kim (Security)

Summary: Quick discovery to validate networking requirements for a Private/VPC deployment. Emerald runs primarily in AWS (us-east-1 + eu-west-1), needs EU data residency, evaluates VPC peering vs PrivateLink, concerned about KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and latency for vessels sending telemetry. Discussed Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and next steps for a POC.

Topics: private endpoints, VPC peering, transit gateway, PrivateLink, region constraints, KMS/HSM, SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, routing/failover, benching throughput and tail latency

[00:00] Carlos: hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm carlos from redwood, and i have priya, our systems engineer, with me. quick round-robin?
[00:12] Lena: hi lena here, CTO at emerald marine. we've got markus and sara on the line. thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Markus: yeah hi, glad to be here.
[00:22] Sara: hi.
[00:25] Priya: great, i'll give a short recap of what we usually see for private deployments and then we can dive into network specifics.

[00:35] Priya: so the two patterns folks choose: one is VPC peering/Transit Gateway with routing to our private subnets, the other is PrivateLink/Private endpoints where we expose an interface endpoint into your VPC. each has tradeoffs around routing, cross-account transits, and egress flow.
[00:53] Markus: can you say a bit more about the difference for egress? like do requests egress to public internet from within your control plane? we have strict egress rules.
[01:05] Priya: sure. with PrivateLink the data path stays within aws networking via interface endpoints, so you don't need to open outbound internet. with peering/transit you have route table entries and sometimes a NAT hop depending on setup — that can be made private but it's more networking work on the customer's side. we also support configuring static routes on our side to your transit gateway if needed.
[01:35] Lena: our hard requirement is no customer data leaving eu for eu workloads; also we need all keys to be customer-managed KMS, ideally HSM-backed. do you support custom KMS?
[01:48] Carlos: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and in private deployments you can bring your own KMS or HSM. priya, do you want to add the implementation note?
[01:58] Priya: yeah. for private deployments we integrate with your KMS over the control plane connection. in aws it's typical to use IAM roles plus KMS grants; for more sensitive workloads we can configure HSM-backed CMKs and log the KMS calls in audit logs. small note: there's sometimes extra latency on key unwraps but it's negligible for token-level ops.
[02:20] Sara: what about audit logs and retention? we need immutable audit trails for model access and admin ops.
[02:27] Priya: we emit audit logs to a customer-owned s3 or to your logging endpoint; retention is configurable, and we can support pushing to a SIEM over kinesis or datadog. we also provide opaque request IDs in logs for traceability.
[02:40] Sara: ok. any certifications? we need SOC 2 type 2 evidence for the procurement process.
[02:46] Carlos: we have SOC 2 and ISO27001 artifacts we can share — i'll include the security pack in the follow-up.

[03:00] Markus: region questions: we run critical fleet telemetry in eu-west-1 and some US control in us-east-1. do you run private control planes in both regions? latency to ships is rough but inland apps need <150ms.
[03:15] Priya: we can deploy private control planes in the region you prefer. for EU-only data we would provision instances and private endpoints in eu-west-1. for cross-region traffic we recommend either peering across your transit gateway or keeping a regional separation: EU traffic stays in eu-west-1 and US in us-east-1. we also support automatic failover to a secondary region but you'll want to confirm data residency rules if you failover.
[03:45] Lena: what's the overhead of keeping two regional deployments? costs, sync, model versions?
[03:52] Carlos: there's some overhead — storage for model weights and model artifacts needs to be in both regions or use a shared replication strategy. Dedicated reserved capacity pricing applies per-region. Priya can share a delta TCO.

[04:10] Priya: on the model side we support model version pinning and rollouts per region. our runtime can run on dedicated gpu pools in each region. if you want the lowest latency to vessels in the EU, put that region's pool in eu-west-1.

[04:30] Markus: on peering: we use a Transit Gateway and strict CIDR ranges. we don't want overlapping CIDRs. what is the CIDR you plan to use on redwood side for private subnets?
[04:40] Priya: by default we recommend using a /20 block, for example 10.240.0.0/20, but it's flexible. we'll coordinate to avoid overlap. if you use a transit gateway we can advertise route propagation to your TGW.
[04:57] Markus: and do you support route tables for ingress filtering? we try to limit ports.
[05:02] Priya: yes, we support security group-like controls on our endpoint side and you can lock down ports. typical is HTTPS 443 only for API traffic. we also support mTLS for service-to-service if you want an extra layer.

[05:20] Lena: about PrivateLink vs peering — we prefer a model where cloud vendors do not require us to manage long-lived peering relationships per vendor. PrivateLink looks cleaner, but i've heard it's more expensive.
[05:31] Priya: correct, PrivateLink can be more operationally simple (interface endpoints, no route table changes), but aws charges for data processing on interface endpoints and for the ENIs. peering/transit may be cheaper at scale but requires more network ops. for some customers we do a hybrid: PrivateLink for control plane and peering for high-throughput batch workloads.

[05:58] Markus: our telemetry streams are high throughput — up to 200 rps bursts translating to spikes in token generation for summarization. can you support bursty workloads?
[06:08] Priya: yes — We have autoscaling for the runtime. in Private deployments you can configure min/max pool sizes, burst capacity, and warm pools for predictable latency. we also support prefix caching so repeated vessel prompts hit the cache and lower token costs.

[06:30] Sara: security question: SSO and RBAC. we use Okta and SCIM for user provisioning. how do admin controls work in the private deployment?
[06:40] Carlos: we integrate with SAML/Okta for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is configurable per-role; in private we can map your IdP groups to Redwood roles. admin audit actions are logged and exported.

[06:56] Lena: any gotchas around peering across accounts or if you need to be in our partner account?
[07:03] Priya: for peering we typically ask customers to create a peering/TGW attachment on their side and share the attachment ID. for PrivateLink we create a service in our account and you create an interface endpoint in yours; that avoids cross-account route complexity. if you prefer, we can be in a partner account model where we operate the private subnet and you accept peering — either works.

[07:28] Markus: curious about public IP egress — some of our network inspectors block unknown external endpoints. will we see traffic to public endpoints during operations?
[07:36] Priya: in private mode you should not see egress to the public internet for API traffic. there may be control plane telemetry to our monitoring if you accept it, but we can also ship metrics to your syslog/kinesis. we'll share a list of endpoints to allow.

[07:55] Lena: what's the typical timeline for private deployment? if we sign a contract how long until we have the control plane in our VPC?
[08:03] Carlos: typical lead time is 4–6 weeks: network setup, key exchange, provisioning, and smoke tests. faster if you already have TGW setup and provide required info quickly. for Dedicated reserved capacity there's a bit more capacity planning but timeline is similar.

[08:20] Markus: for the POC we'd like to benchmark latency for eu-west-1 and us-east-1 and validate throughput with our burst patterns. will you run bench tooling inside our VPC?
[08:30] Priya: yes we can run controlled perf runs from within your VPC using a test harness or we can provide a small agent you run in your environment. we'll want a couple sample prompts and typical sequence lengths to model.

[08:45] Lena: do you support model quantization or custom model images? we have some internal models we might serve.
[08:53] Priya: private supports curated open models and also bringing your own model binaries (BYOM) for private and dedicated. quantization profiles are supported — we can recommend q4/q8 profiles depending on latency and accuracy tradeoffs. note that BYOM has additional security review steps.

[09:10] Markus: anything special about KV cache — we rely on KV cache for long sessions.
[09:16] Priya: yep, we have KV cache management in the runtime; in private deployment the cache can be colocated on the same GPU nodes to reduce latency. there was a small mis-transcription reported in other calls where kv cache was written as kv cash, so just a note.

[09:30] Sara: procurement will ask about indemnity and data processing addenda — can you provide example DPA and security terms?
[09:38] Carlos: absolutely. we'll attach standard DPA, security docs, and can iterate on any legal asks.

[09:50] Lena: about cost — we need a rough TCO comparing hosted (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private in our VPC. how do you normally present that?
[09:59] Carlos: we run a delta TCO: hosted is easiest to start but at your scale Private or Dedicated starts to pay off because of lower per-token execution cost and more control. i'll include an example TCO sheet for both eu and us regions and call out network costs for PrivateLink vs peering.

[10:20] Markus: do you support bringing your own transit gateway? we already have a hub-and-spoke multi-account setup.
[10:27] Priya: yes, we integrate with customer TGWs. we typically ask for TGW attachments or peering details and we'll coordinate route propagation and prefix lists.

[10:40] Lena: any limit on concurrent streams or websocket connections for streaming responses?
[10:46] Priya: streaming is supported; limits depend on the plan and pool sizing. for high concurrency we recommend scaling the runtime pool. we'll show sample throughput numbers in the POC.

[11:00] Markus: internal ops question: who handles upgrades for the runtime? are model updates automated?
[11:07] Carlos: in private deployments we manage the control plane and can automate runtime updates with a rollout policy you approve; model updates are per your version pinning preferences. we can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback.

[11:25] Lena: ok let's talk about the POC scope quickly — we want to validate: 1) latency to vessels (eu region), 2) throughput during bursts, 3) KMS integration and logs, 4) failover behavior. sound right?
[11:38] Priya: that aligns with what we'd typically do. for latency we'll deploy an EU private endpoint and run the harness. for KMS we can set up a test CMK and validate encryption and audit logging. for failover we can simulate region outage and observe behavior.

[11:55] Sara: on failover, if data must not leave eu for compliance, how do you handle cross-region fallback?
[12:02] Priya: we can configure failover to a warm standby in the same region or to another eu region; cross-region failover to us is possible but you'd need to sign off on data movement and usually we keep a geo-fenced policy.

[12:20] Markus: do you guys have any sample terraform for creating interface endpoints and Security group rules?
[12:26] Priya: yes — i'll share Terraform snippets and a sample endpoint template.

[12:36] Carlos: ok cover final logistics — we'll send security pack, network runbook, cost spreadsheet, and proposed POC plan. any blockers from you?
[12:46] Lena: none immediate. procurement will want SOC2 and DPA; security will review KMS/HSM and logging. ops wants the terraform snippets.

[12:57] Markus: i'll pull the CIDR and TGW info and share it.
[13:03] Sara: i'll assemble security requirements and share the regulatory checklist.

[13:12] Carlos: perfect. next steps -- i'll send the deck and the security pack. priya will send the network runbook and terraform. aim to have the POC scheduled mid-april.

[13:25] Lena: thanks, appreciate it.
[13:28] Carlos: thanks all, we'll follow up.
